cleaning_logic: The script reads raw.csv entirely as text (no pandas type/NA inference), strips whitespace from every value, and normalises the missing tokens ('', NA, N/A, null, None, '-', case-insensitive) to NA (R1). It then removes duplicate order_id rows first, keeping the first occurrence in raw-file order, and drops any rows lacking an order_id (R2). Each subsequent rule drops invalid rows in order: order_date is parsed only via the five allowed formats (YYYY-MM-DD, MM/DD/YYYY month-first, DD-Mon-YYYY, YYYY/MM/DD, 'Month D, YYYY') and rewritten as ISO YYYY-MM-DD (R3); region is mapped case-insensitively (including N/S/E/W abbreviations) to North/South/East/West (R4); product_category is mapped case-insensitively, including the specified variants (Electronic, Home and Garden, Home&Garden, Sport, Apparel, Book), to the five canonical categories (R5); unit_price has '$', 'USD' and ',' removed before numeric parsing and must satisfy 0 < price <= 5000 (R6); quantity must parse to a whole number in [1, 50] and is stored as int (R7); discount_pct has a trailing '%' removed, missing values become 0, and values must be in [0, 100] (R8). customer_id is upper-cased with missing set to 'UNKNOWN' (R9). revenue is computed as quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct/100), rounded to 2 decimals (R10). The output contains exactly the nine required columns in order, sorted by order_id ascending, written with a header and no index and plain numeric formatting (R11). cleaning_summary.json records raw_rows, cleaned_rows and per-rule drop/fill counts.
